description: Real, small, popular, known-good model files, verified by SHA-256. Expected MFV scan result for every entry: 0 findings. Not committed to git -- run `scripts/fetch_clean_models.py` to download into cache/ before running the benchmark.

notes.why_pickle_entries_exist: The safetensors entries cannot exercise the pickle engine at all -- safetensors has no opcode stream. Measuring the false-positive rate of MFV-PICKLE-004/005 (the unknown-global bucket and its argument-evidence re-triage) requires real, benign, pickle-format weights, which is what the pytorch_model.bin entries below provide. Filenames are kept exactly as HuggingFace serves them; renaming a .bin to .pt would make it scannable and thereby hide a real coverage gap (see known_gaps).
known_gaps: .bin is not in ModelFileScanner._format_map, so scan_file() returns [] for the three zip-format entries below without reading a byte. pytorch_model.bin is the most common PyTorch weight filename on HuggingFace. These entries currently measure nothing and are here to make that measurable.

sshleifer/tiny-gpt2 is in torch's LEGACY (non-zip) save format: several concatenated pickles, where the real state_dict is pickle #4. _resolve_pickle_globals walks via pickletools.genops, which stops at the first STOP opcode, so only the 14-byte magic-number pickle is examined -- 0.0006% of the file.
